skill.description: Guides an agent through Stripe Projects CLI workflows to browse a service catalog, initialize a project, and provision supported third-party services.

skill.author: stripe

security_audit.summary: Most Markdown backtick detections are false positives because they mark examples, tables, or fixed CLI commands. Real risks remain around package and plugin installation, project initialization, user-controlled CLI arguments, sensitive environment files, and a handoff to a locally installed skill. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before Homebrew installs, Stripe plugin installs, or project initialization. Document the source and expected local changes.
Quote and validate search queries and provider names before constructing shell commands.
State that .env and .projects may be inspected only with explicit consent. Redact secret values from all responses and logs.
Read and review the installed stripe-projects-cli SKILL.md before invoking it in the current workspace.

content.value_statement: Developers often need databases, auth, hosting, and API credentials without leaving their coding workflow. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Stripe Projects CLI provisioning steps.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether the Stripe CLI is installed and reports the installed version.
Installs or updates the Stripe CLI on macOS through Homebrew.
Installs the Stripe Projects plugin and initializes a project.
Searches and browses the Stripe Projects service catalog with JSON output.
Checks project status and lists environment variable names through the CLI.
Hands off to the local stripe-projects-cli skill after initialization.
limitations: Requires the Stripe CLI, Projects plugin, and user authentication.
Can only use providers that appear in the Stripe Projects catalog.
May open browser-based OAuth flows that the user must complete.
Should not reveal secret values from .env or .projects files.

use_cases.title: Add app infrastructure
use_cases.description: Provision a database, cache, auth provider, or hosting service from the Stripe Projects catalog.

use_cases.title: Inspect project setup
use_cases.description: Check initialized project status and list environment variable names without exposing secret values.

use_cases.title: Build an AI service stack
use_cases.description: Find providers for LLM access, vector storage, object storage, search, and email sending.

prompt_templates.title: Browse Available Services
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the Stripe Projects catalog and suggest database options for this app.

prompt_templates.title: Add Required Infrastructure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Stripe Projects to add Postgres and Redis to this project. Show only environment variable names.

prompt_templates.title: Provision an AI Stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Find providers for an LLM, vector database, object storage, and email sending. Compare available options before provisioning.

prompt_templates.title: Recover a Project Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my Stripe Projects status, confirm the local CLI skill is available, and diagnose any provider linking errors.

output_examples.input: I need a database for my prototype.
output_examples.output: The skill searches the catalog, confirms available database providers, initializes the project if needed, and adds the selected service.
The skill checks project status and reports provider names, service types, tiers, and environment variable names only.

output_examples.input: I need an API key for an email provider.
output_examples.output: The skill searches email providers in the catalog and starts the approved provisioning or linking flow.

best_practices: Complete browser authentication before asking the agent to continue.
Ask for environment variable names, not secret values.
Confirm provider choices and tiers before provisioning paid services.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the agent to print .env secret values.
Do not provision services without confirming cost, region, and tier.
Do not hand edit .projects or generated environment files.

faq.question: Does this skill create cloud resources?
faq.answer: Yes. It can run Stripe Projects CLI flows that provision or connect supported third-party services.

faq.question: Does it work without the Stripe CLI?
faq.answer: No. The skill requires the Stripe CLI and the Projects plugin before provisioning can continue.

faq.question: Can it retrieve API credentials?
faq.answer: It can help configure environment variables, but responses should show names only. Secret values should stay redacted.

faq.question: Can it browse the service catalog?
faq.answer: Yes. It can search or browse the Stripe Projects catalog before selecting a provider.

faq.question: What happens when authentication is needed?
faq.answer: The CLI may open a browser. The user must complete sign-in before the agent continues.

faq.question: Is it compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
